dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Mr. Brown, what's the difference between "say" and "tell"?
dialogue.reading: ˈmɪstər ˈbraʊn, ˈwʌts ðə ˈdɪfrəns bɪˈtwiːn ˈseɪ ənd ˈtɛl?

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: We say something, but we tell someone something. For example, "Tell me your name."
dialogue.reading: wiː ˈseɪ ˈsʌmθɪŋ, bʌt wiː ˈtɛl ˈsʌmwʌn ˈsʌmθɪŋ. fər ɪɡˈzæmpəl, ˈtɛl miː jʊr ˈneɪm.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: So I can say, "He told me the answer"?
dialogue.reading: soʊ aɪ kən ˈseɪ, hiː ˈtoʊld miː ði ˈænsər?

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Yes. But you can't say, "He said me the answer."
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs. bʌt juː ˈkænt ˈseɪ, hiː ˈsɛd miː ði ˈænsər.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: What about "speak" and "talk"? What do they mean?
dialogue.reading: ˈwʌt əˈbaʊt ˈspiːk ənd ˈtɔːk? ˈwʌt duː ðeɪ ˈmiːn?

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Their meanings are very similar. We often use "speak" for languages: "I speak Thai."
dialogue.reading: ðɛr ˈmiːnɪŋz ər ˈvɛri ˈsɪmələr. wiː ˈɔːfən ˈjuːz ˈspiːk fər ˈlæŋɡwɪdʒɪz: aɪ ˈspiːk ˈtaɪ.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: We usually use "talk" for a conversation: "Let's talk about it."
dialogue.reading: wiː ˈjuːʒuəli ˈjuːz ˈtɔːk fər ə ˌkɑːnvərˈseɪʃən: ˈlɛts ˈtɔːk əˈbaʊt ɪt.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Sometimes I can't express my ideas in English.
dialogue.reading: ˈsʌmtaɪmz aɪ ˈkænt ɪkˈsprɛs maɪ aɪˈdiːəz ɪn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Then describe them with easy words. That's a good skill, too.
dialogue.reading: ˈðɛn dɪˈskraɪb ðɛm wɪð ˈiːzi ˈwɜːrdz. ðæts ə ˈɡʊd ˈskɪl, ˈtuː.
